name: PostHog
description: PostHog is an open-source product analytics platform combining event tracking, funnels, session recording, feature flags, and A/B testing in a single tool. It can be self-hosted for full data ownership or used as a managed cloud service, making it the preferred choice for privacy-conscious teams and developers who want full control over their analytics stack.

useCases.task: Track user events and build product analytics funnels
Record user sessions to understand how users interact with your UI
Roll out features gradually with feature flags
Run A/B tests to measure feature impact
Self-host analytics for GDPR compliance or data residency requirements

setupSteps: Sign up at posthog.com (or self-host via Docker/Kubernetes)
Create a new project in the PostHog dashboard
Copy your Project API Key from Project Settings > Project API Key
Install the PostHog SDK for your platform
Set POSTHOG_API_KEY and POSTHOG_HOST environment variables

pricing.freeTier: 1,000,000 events/month free, unlimited projects, session recordings included
pricing.costPer: $0.00005 per event above 1M/month; session recordings: $0.005/recording above 5,000 free

rateLimits.limit: No documented API rate limit for event ingestion; batch events to be safe
rateLimits.notes: PostHog is designed for high-volume event ingestion. Use the SDK's built-in batching (default batch size: 20 events, flush interval: 10s) rather than sending individual events.
rateLimits.retryStrategy: PostHog Node SDK handles retries automatically. For self-hosted setups, events queue locally and retry on network failures.

codeExamples.title: Track events and identify users (server-side)
codeExamples.notes: Always call posthog.shutdown() before the process exits (e.g., in serverless/edge functions) to flush the event queue. In long-running servers, the SDK auto-flushes on interval. Use distinctId consistently — it ties all events to one user.

gotchas: PostHog Node SDK batches events and flushes asynchronously — in serverless functions (Vercel, AWS Lambda), the process may exit before events are sent. Always call `await posthog.shutdown()` at the end of serverless handlers, or use `await posthog.flushAsync()`.

The free 1M events/month sounds huge, but session recordings count separately and can add up quickly if you have many users. Session recordings are $0.005 each above 5,000/month — audit your recording settings and consider sampling.

Feature flags are evaluated server-side by calling the PostHog API on each request unless you use local evaluation. Enable local evaluation (requires downloading the flag config) to avoid latency on every request.

Self-hosting PostHog requires significant infrastructure (ClickHouse, Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL). The all-in-one Docker Compose setup works for small scale but needs ~4GB RAM minimum. The cloud version is much easier to start with.

reliability.uptimeGuarantee: 99.9% uptime on cloud; self-hosted depends on your infrastructure
reliability.notes: PostHog cloud (US and EU regions) has strong reliability. The SDK is designed to fail silently — analytics errors should never break your application.

qualityJustification: Best product analytics platform with the most generous free tier (1M events/month). The combination of event tracking, session recording, feature flags, and A/B testing in one SDK is a genuine differentiator. Open-source and self-hostable for data control. The only drawbacks are self-hosting complexity and the serverless flush gotcha.
bestFor: Product analytics, feature flags, and session recording with a generous free tier and optional self-hosting for data ownership
